skill.name: reconnaissance-knowledge
skill.description: A reconnaissance knowledge base for authorized security work. It explains layered port discovery, service enumeration, web discovery, and structured reporting workflows.
skill.summary: Guides authorized reconnaissance planning, service inventory, and structured findings reports.
skill.author: CharlesKozel

security_audit.summary: The Markdown command-format detections are mostly false positives for code formatting, but the blocker findings are confirmed. The skill provides actionable network reconnaissance workflows, stealth scanning advice, default credential probing, and exploitation handoff guidance.

remediation.issue: Actionable active reconnaissance commands and tool playbooks are provided without enforceable scope checks.
remediation.suggestion: Limit the skill to planning and reporting guidance, and require explicit authorization, scope, timing, and rate limits before any active command is discussed.

remediation.issue: Stealth scanning guidance is included for real environments.
remediation.suggestion: Remove stealth or evasion language and replace it with safe rate-limit and change-window guidance for authorized owners.

remediation.issue: Default credential testing and exploitation handoff instructions expand beyond passive reconnaissance.
remediation.suggestion: Remove credential probing and exploitation transition language, or gate it behind explicit authorized assessment context.

content.value_statement: Security teams need structured ways to inventory authorized targets. This skill organizes reconnaissance phases, evidence capture, and reporting for controlled assessments.
actual_capabilities: Explains layered reconnaissance phases from port discovery to service inventory.
Lists common tools for port scanning, web enumeration, DNS checks, and service checks.
Provides structured fields for ports, services, technologies, paths, and vulnerabilities.
Describes escalation from quick checks to deeper authorized enumeration.
Outlines handoff details for later security assessment phases.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not enforce authorization or scope limits.
It includes commands that can affect real networks if used outside permission.
It does not validate target ownership, rate limits, or legal approval.
It can identify potential issues but does not confirm exploitability.

use_cases.title: Plan an Authorized Lab Reconnaissance Pass
use_cases.description: Build a phased checklist for a training range or controlled target before deeper testing.

use_cases.title: Normalize Service Inventory Notes
use_cases.description: Turn scattered reconnaissance observations into a consistent inventory for team review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Assessment Handoff Material
use_cases.description: Summarize discovered services, technologies, and potential follow-up areas for an authorized engagement.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Recon Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an authorized lab target.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe reconnaissance checklist for an authorized lab target. Include phases, evidence to capture, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Service Findings
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert notes into a clear inventory.
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize these authorized reconnaissance notes into ports, services, versions, web technologies, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Next Enumeration Steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Decide how to deepen an approved assessment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this authorized service inventory, suggest bounded next enumeration steps and explain the purpose of each step.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Recon Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reporting for a controlled engagement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a concise reconnaissance handoff for an authorized assessment. Include evidence, confidence, risks, and required approvals before follow-up testing.

output_examples.input: A target has open SSH and HTTP services with an outdated web platform.
output_examples.output: The result separates service inventory, observed technologies, evidence quality, and follow-up questions for the assessment owner.

output_examples.input: A web scan found admin paths, uploads paths, and several redirects.
output_examples.output: The result groups paths by status, notes potential business impact, and lists safe validation steps for authorized review.

output_examples.input: A team needs a final reconnaissance handoff before deeper testing.
output_examples.output: The result summarizes discovered services, notable risks, unresolved questions, and approval gates for the next phase.

best_practices: Use the skill only inside explicit written authorization and defined scope.
Record evidence, timestamps, assumptions, and target identifiers for every finding.
Prefer bounded checks and stop when results suggest impact beyond the approved scope.
anti_patterns: Do not scan public or third-party networks without written permission.
Do not use stealth guidance to evade monitoring or hide activity.
Do not treat suggested vulnerabilities as confirmed without approved validation.

faq.question: Does this skill run scans by itself?
faq.answer: No. It is a knowledge base, but it includes commands that an agent or user could run.

faq.question: Is this safe for production networks?
faq.answer: Only with explicit authorization, scope, timing, and rate limits from the network owner.

faq.question: Can it confirm vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize reconnaissance and identify areas that may need approved validation.

faq.question: Why is marketplace review strict for this skill?
faq.answer: The skill teaches network scanning, service enumeration, default credential checks, and exploitation handoff planning.

faq.question: What tools does it discuss?
faq.answer: It discusses tools such as nmap, masscan, gobuster, nikto, enum4linux, and DNS utilities.

faq.question: Who is the intended user?
faq.answer: The intended user is a security practitioner working in an authorized lab or controlled assessment.
